content.text:
Facts verified in this directory before reviewing (I read AGENTS.md, `../../prompts/L3.md`, the CSV, and the venv):

- Data: 50,400 rows, strictly hourly, monotonic, no duplicates, no NaN, range 31,307 to 77,549 MW. The integrity check will pass; nothing to report.
- Venv: darts 0.41.0, lightgbm 4.6.0, statsmodels 0.14.6, holidays 0.96, torch 2.10. `PatchTSTModel` is absent; `TransformerModel` exists (a real encoder-decoder transformer), so the substitution is correct. `NBEATSModel.fit` natively accepts `stride=` and `max_samples_per_ts=`; `predict` accepts `predict_likelihood_parameters=True`. `MLEResults.apply(endog, refit=False)` exists for fixed-coefficient state updates. `holidays.Germany()` without subdiv is national-only; Jan 6 2020 is not in it.
- Arithmetic: Oct 1 + 13 x 168 h = Dec 31 00:00, so 13 blocks + a 24 h block = 2208 h exactly.

Findings, most serious first.

1. Deep-model early stopping is not what Darts gives you by default. `EarlyStopping` monitors `val_loss` (the likelihood loss on stride-1 val windows), not MAPE over your 14 origins. To honour the design you need a Lightning callback that at each epoch end runs 14 predictions from the actual-history origins and records median-MAPE, then pick the argmin epoch. If you fall back to `val_loss`, say so; do not describe it as "validation MAPE". Also prepend the last 168 h of train to the val series or the first val target window starts Oct 8, not Oct 1.

2. Prophet has no state, so "val history updates contexts" is vacuous for it: every validation block is scored from one fit ending Sep 30 at 1 to 92 days ahead, while every other model is scored at 1 to 168 h ahead. That is legitimate for Prophet's own hyperparameter choice (it is never compared across models on val), but disclose that its val MAPE is not comparable, and name the grid (e.g. changepoint_prior_scale x seasonality_mode, holidays_prior_scale). Refit-per-block is not an option under the prompt's "no data after Sep 30 during sweeps" rule.

3. LightGBM quantile recursion: state explicitly that all five quantile models are fed the same recursive path built from the q0.5 (or L2 point) predictions; recursing each quantile on its own outputs produces a compounding fan that is not a conditional quantile. Also the recursive rolling-std feature will collapse (predictions are smoother than actuals), a distribution shift you should name. And run the validation scoring in recursive mode, not one-step-ahead with actual lags, or you tune the wrong task. Note lag_8760 forces dropping 2015 from the LightGBM training set (train becomes ~3.75 y); 8760 h back from 2020-01-01 lands on 2019-01-01 (holiday-aligned, weekday off by one), 8736 h gives weekday alignment. Pick one and record.

4. Stride and origin alignment: Darts indexes training windows from the series end, and both train (ends Sep 30 23:00) and train+val (ends Dec 31 23:00) end at 23:00 UTC, so stride=24 restricts training origins to 00:00 UTC, which is exactly the test origin. That is a feature, but say it, and use the same stride in selection and refit. Also with a quantile likelihood the "point forecast" is the q0.5 output; state that, and use `predict_likelihood_parameters=True` for coverage rather than sampled quantiles. Drop "distribution outputs" from the design; one likelihood, quantile regression, for both deep models.

5. Timezone in Prophet: Darts needs a regular index, so the series stays UTC and `country_holidays="DE"` marks holidays by UTC date, one hour off Berlin midnight. Small, but it also means Prophet's fixed daily Fourier is fitted in UTC across DST, blurring the profile. Disclose; a conditional summer/winter daily seasonality is an allowed fix if you want it.

6. The 24 h Dec 31 block mixes horizons 1 to 24 into a pool otherwise at 1 to 168. It is 1% of val hours, so pooled MAPE is fine; just do not treat it as a 14th equal block if you report per-block dispersion (n=13 is already a small selection sample; report the spread).

7. Naive fallback intervals: pooled signed-error quantiles over the 2208 val hours are defensible (every naive val forecast is a genuine 1 to 168 h ahead value). Note val contains Christmas week, so the intervals will be wide; test coverage is then an honest out-of-sample check of the layer. Label it in `hyperparameters` as an auxiliary calibration, as you propose. Optionally offer per-hour-of-day quantiles as a variant, not a default.

8. Naming of the sixth model: the schema enumerates `patchtst`. Using that name for `TransformerModel` mislabels in the other direction. Recommend `name: "transformer"` in metrics and figures, file kept as `code/patchtst.py` per the layout, substitution recorded in transcript. Flag as a deliberate schema deviation.

9. SARIMAX cost: s=24 seasonal MA terms on 41,600 obs run minutes each in statsmodels; keep the explicit candidate set to about 4 to 6 orders and record the budget. Analytic intervals assume Gaussian innovations and ignore parameter uncertainty; say so. Timestamp-derived exog (weekly Fourier terms, Berlin holiday dummy) is allowed by the prompt and would directly address Jan 1; not required, but the design should say why it is omitted if it is.

10. Minor: Jan 6 (Epiphany, regional) falls on the test Monday and is excluded by national-only; Jan 2 to 3 are bridge days no calendar feature captures; the naive's Jan 2 forecast is Dec 26 (a holiday). These belong in the discussion, not in the pipeline. Metric figure: the naive=1 normalisation deviates from the prompt's literal "three grouped bars"; a 1x3 panel with raw axes is the more conventional fix, but either is acceptable if raw values are labelled and the full table is present. Keep CPU (not MPS) for the torch models unless runtime forces otherwise, and record seeds; even with seeds, the refit will not reproduce the selection run's weights exactly.

Sanity check: I re-read the ask (review only, no edits, no subagents, no training); I wrote nothing, spawned nothing, and only ran read-only probes of the CSV and library signatures.

result: Bake-off design is sound; ten concrete challenges returned, chiefly that Darts early stopping does not natively give per-origin validation MAPE, Prophet's validation is a 92-day horizon, LightGBM quantile recursion must share the median path, and the transformer substitute should not be named patchtst.

from __future__ import annotations

import gc
import logging
import time
from typing import Any

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import torch
from darts import TimeSeries
from darts.models import NBEATSModel
from darts.utils.likelihood_models import QuantileRegression
from pytorch_lightning import Callback, LightningModule, Trainer, seed_everything

from common import HORIZON, ModelResult, QUANTILES, ROOT, SEED, mape, validation_blocks


class ValidationMAPE(Callback):
    def __init__(self, train: pd.Series, pretest: pd.Series, scale: float) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        blocks = validation_blocks(pretest, len(train))
        self.context = torch.tensor(np.stack([h.iloc[-HORIZON:].to_numpy() / scale for h, _ in blocks]),
                                    dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(-1)
        self.targets = pretest.iloc[len(train):].to_numpy()
        self.lengths = [len(target) for _, target in blocks]
        self.scale = scale
        self.best_mape = float("inf")
        self.best_epoch = 0
        self.best_prediction = np.empty(0)
        self.history: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        self.stale = 0
        self.significant_best = float("inf")

    def on_train_epoch_end(self, trainer: Trainer, pl_module: LightningModule) -> None:
        was_training = pl_module.training
        pl_module.eval()
        with torch.inference_mode():
            output = pl_module((self.context.to(pl_module.device), None, None))
            q = np.sort(output[:, :, 0, :].detach().cpu().numpy(), axis=2) * self.scale
        pl_module.train(was_training)
        point = np.concatenate([q[i, :length, 2] for i, length in enumerate(self.lengths)])
        score = mape(self.targets, point)
        epoch = trainer.current_epoch + 1
        self.history.append({"epoch": epoch, "validation_mape_pct": score})
        print(f"{type(pl_module).__name__} epoch={epoch} validation MAPE={score:.3f}%", flush=True)
        if score < self.best_mape:
            self.best_mape = score
            self.best_epoch = epoch
            self.best_prediction = point.copy()
        if score < self.significant_best - 0.01:
            self.significant_best = score
            self.stale = 0
        else:
            self.stale += 1
        if self.stale >= 5:
            trainer.should_stop = True


def make_model(model_class: Any, epochs: int, callbacks: list[Callback], name: str,
               architecture: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
    return model_class(
        input_chunk_length=168, output_chunk_length=168,
        n_epochs=epochs, batch_size=32, random_state=SEED,
        likelihood=QuantileRegression(quantiles=QUANTILES),
        optimizer_kwargs={"lr": 0.001}, save_checkpoints=False,
        force_reset=True, work_dir=str(ROOT / ".cache" / "darts"), model_name=name,
        pl_trainer_kwargs={"accelerator": "cpu", "devices": 1,
                           "enable_progress_bar": False, "enable_model_summary": False,
                           "logger": False, "enable_checkpointing": False,
                           "deterministic": True, "gradient_clip_val": 1.0,
                           "callbacks": callbacks, "num_sanity_val_steps": 0},
        **architecture,
    )


def series(y: pd.Series, scale: float) -> TimeSeries:
    return TimeSeries.from_series((y / scale).astype(np.float32), freq="h")


def run_neural(name: str, model_class: Any, architecture: dict[str, Any],
               train: pd.Series, pretest: pd.Series, future: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> ModelResult:
    start = time.perf_counter()
    torch.set_num_threads(4)
    torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)
    logging.getLogger("pytorch_lightning").setLevel(logging.WARNING)
    seed_everything(SEED, workers=True, verbose=False)
    train_scale = float(train.mean())
    callback = ValidationMAPE(train, pretest, train_scale)
    model = make_model(model_class, 30, [callback], f"{name}_selection", architecture)
    model.fit(series(train, train_scale), stride=168, verbose=False,
              dataloader_kwargs={"num_workers": 0})
    selected_epochs = callback.best_epoch
    if selected_epochs < 1:
        raise RuntimeError("Neural validation callback did not run.")
    del model
    gc.collect()
    # This is a fresh fit, not continued optimization on validation targets.
    seed_everything(SEED, workers=True, verbose=False)
    final_scale = float(pretest.mean())
    final = make_model(model_class, selected_epochs, [], f"{name}_final", architecture)
    final_series = series(pretest, final_scale)
    final.fit(final_series, stride=168, verbose=False, dataloader_kwargs={"num_workers": 0})
    distribution = final.predict(len(future), series=final_series,
                                 predict_likelihood_parameters=True, num_samples=1, verbose=False)
    if not distribution.time_index.equals(future):
        raise ValueError("Darts returned an unexpected test forecast index.")
    quantiles = np.sort(distribution.values(), axis=1).astype(float) * final_scale
    # The callback's fast forward path must agree with the public Darts predictor.
    final.model.eval()
    context = torch.tensor(final_series.values()[-168:], dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(0)
    with torch.inference_mode():
        raw = final.model((context, None, None))[0, :, 0, :].cpu().numpy()
    np.testing.assert_allclose(np.sort(raw, axis=1) * final_scale, quantiles, rtol=2e-5, atol=0.1)
    params = {"actual_class": model_class.__name__, "input_chunk_length": 168,
              "output_chunk_length": 168, "max_epochs": 30, "selected_epochs": selected_epochs,
              "early_stopping_metric": "validation MAPE of rearranged median, all 2208 hours",
              "early_stopping_patience": 5, "early_stopping_min_delta_pct": 0.01,
              "training_stride_hours": 168, "batch_size": 32, "learning_rate": 0.001,
              "gradient_clip_val": 1.0, "likelihood": "QuantileRegression",
              "quantiles": QUANTILES, "seed": SEED, "accelerator": "cpu", "threads": 4,
              "train_scale_mw": train_scale, "final_scale_mw": final_scale,
              "final_training_windows": (len(pretest) - 336) // 168 + 1,
              **architecture}
    if name == "nbeats":
        params.update({"generic_architecture": True, "num_stacks": 30, "num_blocks": 1,
                       "num_layers": 4, "layer_widths": 256, "expansion_coefficient_dim": 5})
    else:
        params["substitution"] = "Darts 0.41.0 has no PatchTSTModel; TransformerModel is an actual transformer, not TSMixer."
    result = ModelResult(name, quantiles[:, 2], quantiles, callback.best_prediction,
                         params, callback.history, time.perf_counter() - start,
                         {"callback_public_predict_equivalence": True})
    del final
    gc.collect()
    return result


def run(train: pd.Series, pretest: pd.Series, future: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> ModelResult:
    return run_neural("nbeats", NBEATSModel, {}, train, pretest, future)

        self.history: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        self.stale = 0
        self.significant_best = float("inf")

    def on_train_epoch_end(self, trainer: Trainer, pl_module: LightningModule) -> None:
        was_training = pl_module.training
        pl_module.eval()
        with torch.inference_mode():
            output = pl_module((self.context.to(pl_module.device), None, None))
            q = np.sort(output[:, :, 0, :].detach().cpu().numpy(), axis=2) * self.scale
        pl_module.train(was_training)
        point = np.concatenate([q[i, :length, 2] for i, length in enumerate(self.lengths)])
        score = mape(self.targets, point)
        epoch = trainer.current_epoch + 1
        self.history.append({"epoch": epoch, "validation_mape_pct": score})
        print(f"{type(pl_module).__name__} epoch={epoch} validation MAPE={score:.3f}%", flush=True)
        if score < self.best_mape:
            self.best_mape = score
            self.best_epoch = epoch
            self.best_prediction = point.copy()
        if score < self.significant_best - 0.01:
            self.significant_best = score
            self.stale = 0
        else:
            self.stale += 1
        if self.stale >= 5:
            trainer.should_stop = True

               architecture: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
    return model_class(

               train: pd.Series, pretest: pd.Series, future: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> ModelResult:
    start = time.perf_counter()
    torch.set_num_threads(4)

    logging.getLogger("pytorch_lightning").setLevel(logging.WARNING)
    seed_everything(SEED, workers=True, verbose=False)

    callback = ValidationMAPE(train, pretest, train_scale)
    model = make_model(model_class, 30, [callback], f"{name}_selection", architecture)
    model.fit(series(train, train_scale), stride=168, verbose=False,
              dataloader_kwargs={"num_workers": 0})
    selected_epochs = callback.best_epoch
    if selected_epochs < 1:
        raise RuntimeError("Neural validation callback did not run.")
    del model
    gc.collect()

    seed_everything(SEED, workers=True, verbose=False)
    final_scale = float(pretest.mean())
    final = make_model(model_class, selected_epochs, [], f"{name}_final", architecture)
    final_series = series(pretest, final_scale)
    final.fit(final_series, stride=168, verbose=False, dataloader_kwargs={"num_workers": 0})
    distribution = final.predict(len(future), series=final_series,
                                 predict_likelihood_parameters=True, num_samples=1, verbose=False)
    if not distribution.time_index.equals(future):
        raise ValueError("Darts returned an unexpected test forecast index.")
    quantiles = np.sort(distribution.values(), axis=1).astype(float) * final_scale
    # The callback's fast forward path must agree with the public Darts predictor.
    final.model.eval()
    context = torch.tensor(final_series.values()[-168:], dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(0)
    with torch.inference_mode():
        raw = final.model((context, None, None))[0, :, 0, :].cpu().numpy()
    np.testing.assert_allclose(np.sort(raw, axis=1) * final_scale, quantiles, rtol=2e-5, atol=0.1)
    params = {"actual_class": model_class.__name__, "input_chunk_length": 168,
              "output_chunk_length": 168, "max_epochs": 30, "selected_epochs": selected_epochs,
              "early_stopping_metric": "validation MAPE of rearranged median, all 2208 hours",
              "early_stopping_patience": 5, "early_stopping_min_delta_pct": 0.01,
              "training_stride_hours": 168, "batch_size": 32, "learning_rate": 0.001,
              "gradient_clip_val": 1.0, "likelihood": "QuantileRegression",
              "quantiles": QUANTILES, "seed": SEED, "accelerator": "cpu", "threads": 4,
              "train_scale_mw": train_scale, "final_scale_mw": final_scale,
              "final_training_windows": (len(pretest) - 336) // 168 + 1,
              **architecture}
    if name == "nbeats":
        params.update({"generic_architecture": True, "num_stacks": 30, "num_blocks": 1,
                       "num_layers": 4, "layer_widths": 256, "expansion_coefficient_dim": 5})
    else:
        params["substitution"] = "Darts 0.41.0 has no PatchTSTModel; TransformerModel is an actual transformer, not TSMixer."
    result = ModelResult(name, quantiles[:, 2], quantiles, callback.best_prediction,
                         params, callback.history, time.perf_counter() - start,
                         {"callback_public_predict_equivalence": True})
    del final
    gc.collect()
    return result


def run(train: pd.Series, pretest: pd.Series, future: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> ModelResult:
    return run_neural("nbeats", NBEATSModel, {}, train, pretest, future)

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd


def save_result(result: Any, future: pd.DatetimeIndex, validation_index: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> None:
    target = ROOT / "artifacts"
    target.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    forecast = pd.DataFrame({"point": result.point}, index=future)
    if result.quantiles is not None:
        forecast = pd.concat([forecast, common.quantile_frame(result.quantiles, future)], axis=1)

        parser.error("Choose at most one mode.")
    started = time.perf_counter()
    data = common.load_data()

        common.seed_everything()
        for name, filename in zip(common.NAMES, ["naive.py", "sarima.py", "prophet.py", "lightgbm_features.py", "nbeats.py", "patchtst.py"]):
            print(f"START {name}", flush=True)
            module = load_module(f"study_{name}", filename)
            result = module.run(train.copy(), pretest.copy(), future.copy())
            if result.point.shape != (168,) or not np.isfinite(result.point).all():
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid forecast for {name}")
            save_result(result, future, pretest.index[len(train):])
            print(f"DONE {name} runtime_seconds={result.runtime_seconds:.2f}", flush=True)
        versions = {name: importlib.metadata.version(name) for name in
                    ["numpy", "pandas", "matplotlib", "statsmodels", "darts", "lightgbm", "holidays", "torch", "pytorch-lightning", "prophet"]}
        common.dump_json(ROOT / "artifacts" / "run.json", {
            "training_wall_seconds": time.perf_counter() - started, "seed": common.SEED,
            "python": platform.python_version(), "packages": versions,
            "uname": subprocess.check_output(["uname", "-a"], text=True).strip(),
            "machine": platform.machine(), "logical_cpu_count": os.cpu_count(),
            "data_sha256": common.source_digest(), "train_rows": len(train),
            "validation_rows": len(pretest) - len(train), "refit_rows": len(pretest),
            "test_rows": len(future),
        })
    if not args.train_only:
        reporting = load_module("study_reporting", "reporting.py")
        reporting.generate(data, read_results())
    print("ALL_DONE", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

from darts import TimeSeries
from darts.models import Prophet

from common import ModelResult, QUANTILES, SEED, mape


def make_model(mode: str) -> Prophet:
    return Prophet(country_holidays="DE", daily_seasonality=True,
                   weekly_seasonality=True, yearly_seasonality=True,
                   seasonality_mode=mode, changepoint_prior_scale=0.01,
                   holidays_prior_scale=10.0, uncertainty_samples=600,
                   random_state=SEED)


def as_series(y: pd.Series) -> TimeSeries:
    return TimeSeries.from_series(y, fill_missing_dates=False, freq="h")


def run(train: pd.Series, pretest: pd.Series, future: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> ModelResult:
    start = time.perf_counter()
    logging.getLogger("cmdstanpy").setLevel(logging.WARNING)
    candidates: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    forecasts: list[np.ndarray] = []
    validation_frame = pd.DataFrame({"ds": pretest.index[len(train):]})
    for mode in ("additive", "multiplicative"):
        model = make_model(mode)
        model.fit(as_series(train))
        # Prophet's time-only prediction is identical across the fixed-origin blocks.
        prediction = model.model.predict(validation_frame)["yhat"].to_numpy()
        score = mape(pretest.iloc[len(train):].to_numpy(), prediction)
        candidates.append({"seasonality_mode": mode, "validation_mape_pct": score})
        forecasts.append(prediction)
        print(f"prophet mode={mode} validation MAPE={score:.3f}%", flush=True)
    chosen = int(np.argmin([c["validation_mape_pct"] for c in candidates]))
    mode = candidates[chosen]["seasonality_mode"]
    final = make_model(mode)
    final.fit(as_series(pretest))
    frame = pd.DataFrame({"ds": future})
    prediction_frame = final.model.predict(frame)
    np.random.seed(SEED)
    samples = final.model.predictive_samples(frame)["yhat"]
    quantiles = np.quantile(samples, QUANTILES, axis=1).T
    components = prediction_frame[["ds", "trend", "weekly", "yearly", "daily", "holidays"]].copy()

              "seed": SEED, "calendar_timezone": "UTC (library-naive timestamps)",

    return ModelResult("prophet", prediction_frame["yhat"].to_numpy(), quantiles,

from __future__ import annotations

import time
import warnings
from typing import Any

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import norm
from statsmodels.tsa.statespace.sarimax import SARIMAX

from common import ModelResult, QUANTILES, mape, validation_blocks

SCALE = 10000.0


def fit_model(y: pd.Series, order: tuple[int, int, int], seasonal: tuple[int, int, int, int]) -> tuple[Any, list[str]]:
    weekly_difference = (y.diff(168).iloc[168:] / SCALE).asfreq("h")
    model = SARIMAX(weekly_difference, order=order, seasonal_order=seasonal,
                    trend="n", enforce_stationarity=True, enforce_invertibility=True,
                    concentrate_scale=True)
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
        warnings.simplefilter("always")
        fit = model.fit(disp=False, maxiter=60, low_memory=True)
        if not fit.mle_retvals.get("converged", False):
            fit = model.fit(start_params=fit.params, disp=False, maxiter=120, low_memory=True)
    messages = list(dict.fromkeys(str(w.message) for w in caught))
    if not fit.mle_retvals.get("converged", False):
        raise RuntimeError(f"SARIMA optimizer did not converge: {order}, {seasonal}")
    return fit, messages


def run(train: pd.Series, pretest: pd.Series, future: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> ModelResult:
    start = time.perf_counter()
    candidates: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    forecasts: list[np.ndarray] = []
    warnings_seen: list[str] = []
    for order, seasonal in [((1, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0, 24)), ((2, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0, 24))]:
        fit, messages = fit_model(train, order, seasonal)
        warnings_seen.extend(messages)
        prediction: list[np.ndarray] = []
        for history, target in validation_blocks(pretest, len(train)):
            baseline = history.loc[target.index - pd.Timedelta(hours=168)].to_numpy()
            prediction.append(fit.get_forecast(len(target)).predicted_mean.to_numpy() * SCALE + baseline)
            # Only the state is updated as each validation block becomes history.
            observed_difference = pd.Series((target.to_numpy() - baseline) / SCALE, index=target.index).asfreq("h")
            fit = fit.extend(observed_difference)
        point = np.concatenate(prediction)
        score = mape(pretest.iloc[len(train):].to_numpy(), point)
        candidates.append({"order": list(order), "seasonal_order": list(seasonal),
                           "validation_mape_pct": score, "converged": True})
        forecasts.append(point)
        print(f"sarima {order}{seasonal} validation MAPE={score:.3f}%", flush=True)
    chosen = int(np.argmin([c["validation_mape_pct"] for c in candidates]))
    config = candidates[chosen]
    fit, messages = fit_model(pretest, tuple(config["order"]), tuple(config["seasonal_order"]))
    warnings_seen.extend(messages)
    distribution = fit.get_forecast(len(future))
    baseline = pretest.loc[future - pd.Timedelta(hours=168)].to_numpy()
    point = distribution.predicted_mean.to_numpy() * SCALE + baseline
    se = np.asarray(distribution.se_mean) * SCALE
    q = point[:, None] + se[:, None] * norm.ppf(QUANTILES)[None, :]
    params = {"order": config["order"], "seasonal_order": config["seasonal_order"],
              "weekly_pre_difference_hours": 168, "fixed_numeric_scale_mw": SCALE,
              "trend": "none", "concentrate_scale": True, "final_converged": True,
              "uncertainty": "Gaussian forecast-error variance; fixed fitted parameters"}
    return ModelResult("sarima", point, q, forecasts[chosen], params, candidates,
                       time.perf_counter() - start, {"optimizer_warnings": sorted(set(warnings_seen))})

from __future__ import annotations

import time
from typing import Any

import holidays
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from lightgbm import LGBMRegressor

from common import ModelResult, QUANTILES, SEED, mape, validation_blocks

FEATURES = ["hour", "day_of_week", "month", "is_weekend", "is_public_holiday_de",
            "lag_24h", "lag_168h", "lag_8760h", "rolling_mean_24h", "rolling_std_24h",
            "rolling_mean_168h", "rolling_std_168h"]


def calendar(index: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> pd.DataFrame:
    local = index.tz_localize("UTC").tz_convert("Europe/Berlin")
    holiday_dates = holidays.Germany(years=range(local.year.min(), local.year.max() + 1))
    return pd.DataFrame({
        "hour": local.hour, "day_of_week": local.dayofweek, "month": local.month,
        "is_weekend": (local.dayofweek >= 5).astype(int),
        "is_public_holiday_de": [int(day in holiday_dates) for day in local.date],
    }, index=index)


def feature_frame(y: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    x = calendar(y.index)
    for hours in (24, 168, 8760):
        x[f"lag_{hours}h"] = y.shift(hours)
    # Excluding the current target is stricter than merely excluding later rows.
    past = y.shift(1)
    for hours in (24, 168):
        x[f"rolling_mean_{hours}h"] = past.rolling(hours).mean()
        x[f"rolling_std_{hours}h"] = past.rolling(hours).std(ddof=1)
    return x[FEATURES]


def recursive_forecast(models: dict[float, Any], history: pd.Series,
                       future: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> np.ndarray:
    if len(history) < 8760 or future[0] != history.index[-1] + pd.Timedelta(hours=1):
        raise ValueError("Forecast must follow a complete history with all lags available.")
    if not future.equals(pd.date_range(future[0], periods=len(future), freq="h")):
        raise ValueError("Forecast timestamps must be contiguous hourly instants.")
    known: list[float] = history.to_list()
    time_values = calendar(future).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    quantiles = sorted(models)
    result = np.empty((len(future), len(quantiles)))
    for i in range(len(future)):
        row = list(time_values[i]) + [known[-lag] for lag in (24, 168, 8760)]
        for hours in (24, 168):
            window = np.asarray(known[-hours:])
            row.extend([float(window.mean()), float(window.std(ddof=1))])
        x = pd.DataFrame([row], columns=FEATURES)
        prediction = np.array([models[q].predict(x)[0] for q in quantiles])
        result[i] = np.sort(prediction)
        known.append(float(result[i, quantiles.index(0.5)]))
    return result


def estimator(leaves: int, quantile: float) -> LGBMRegressor:
    return LGBMRegressor(objective="quantile", alpha=quantile, n_estimators=300,
                         learning_rate=0.05, num_leaves=leaves, min_child_samples=60,
                         reg_lambda=1.0, random_state=SEED, n_jobs=1, verbosity=-1,
                         deterministic=True, force_col_wise=True)


def run(train: pd.Series, pretest: pd.Series, future: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> ModelResult:
    start = time.perf_counter()
    x = feature_frame(train).iloc[8760:]
    y = train.iloc[8760:]
    candidates: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    forecasts: list[np.ndarray] = []
    for leaves in (15, 31):
        model = estimator(leaves, 0.5).fit(x, y)
        prediction = np.concatenate([recursive_forecast({0.5: model}, history, target.index)[:, 0]
                                     for history, target in validation_blocks(pretest, len(train))])
        score = mape(pretest.iloc[len(train):].to_numpy(), prediction)
        candidates.append({"num_leaves": leaves, "validation_mape_pct": score})
        forecasts.append(prediction)
        print(f"lightgbm leaves={leaves} validation MAPE={score:.3f}%", flush=True)
    chosen = int(np.argmin([c["validation_mape_pct"] for c in candidates]))
    leaves = candidates[chosen]["num_leaves"]
    final_x = feature_frame(pretest).iloc[8760:]
    models = {q: estimator(leaves, q).fit(final_x, pretest.iloc[8760:]) for q in QUANTILES}
    quantiles = recursive_forecast(models, pretest, future)
    importance = dict(zip(FEATURES, models[0.5].booster_.feature_importance(importance_type="gain").tolist()))
    params = {"num_leaves": leaves, "n_estimators": 300, "learning_rate": 0.05,
              "min_child_samples": 60, "reg_lambda": 1.0, "quantiles": QUANTILES,
              "seed": SEED, "features": FEATURES, "calendar_timezone": "Europe/Berlin",
              "training_feature_warmup_hours": 8760, "final_training_rows": len(final_x),
              "forecast_method": "recursive, quantile rearrangement at each step",
              "uncertainty": "conditional quantiles on recursive median predictor path"}
    return ModelResult("lightgbm", quantiles[:, 2], quantiles, forecasts[chosen], params,
                       candidates, time.perf_counter() - start, {"feature_importance_gain": importance})

import time
from typing import Any

import holidays
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from lightgbm import LGBMRegressor

from common import ModelResult, QUANTILES, SEED, mape, validation_blocks

FEATURES = ["hour", "day_of_week", "month", "is_weekend", "is_public_holiday_de",
            "lag_24h", "lag_168h", "lag_8760h", "rolling_mean_24h", "rolling_std_24h",
            "rolling_mean_168h", "rolling_std_168h"]


def calendar(index: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> pd.DataFrame:
    local = index.tz_localize("UTC").tz_convert("Europe/Berlin")
    holiday_dates = holidays.Germany(years=range(local.year.min(), local.year.max() + 1))
    return pd.DataFrame({
        "hour": local.hour, "day_of_week": local.dayofweek, "month": local.month,
        "is_weekend": (local.dayofweek >= 5).astype(int),
        "is_public_holiday_de": [int(day in holiday_dates) for day in local.date],
    }, index=index)


def feature_frame(y: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    x = calendar(y.index)
    for hours in (24, 168, 8760):
        x[f"lag_{hours}h"] = y.shift(hours)
    # Excluding the current target is stricter than merely excluding later rows.
    past = y.shift(1)
    for hours in (24, 168):
        x[f"rolling_mean_{hours}h"] = past.rolling(hours).mean()
        x[f"rolling_std_{hours}h"] = past.rolling(hours).std(ddof=1)
    return x[FEATURES]


def recursive_forecast(models: dict[float, Any], history: pd.Series,
                       future: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> np.ndarray:
    if len(history) < 8760 or future[0] != history.index[-1] + pd.Timedelta(hours=1):
        raise ValueError("Forecast must follow a complete history with all lags available.")
    if not future.equals(pd.date_range(future[0], periods=len(future), freq="h")):
        raise ValueError("Forecast timestamps must be contiguous hourly instants.")
    known: list[float] = history.to_list()
    time_values = calendar(future).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    quantiles = sorted(models)
    result = np.empty((len(future), len(quantiles)))
    for i in range(len(future)):
        row = list(time_values[i]) + [known[-lag] for lag in (24, 168, 8760)]
        for hours in (24, 168):
            window = np.asarray(known[-hours:])
            row.extend([float(window.mean()), float(window.std(ddof=1))])
        x = pd.DataFrame([row], columns=FEATURES)
        prediction = np.array([models[q].predict(x)[0] for q in quantiles])
        median_index = quantiles.index(0.5)
        median = prediction[median_index]
        result[i, :median_index] = np.minimum(np.sort(prediction[:median_index]), median)
        result[i, median_index] = median
        result[i, median_index + 1:] = np.maximum(np.sort(prediction[median_index + 1:]), median)
        known.append(float(median))

def run(train: pd.Series, pretest: pd.Series, future: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> ModelResult:
    start = time.perf_counter()
    x = feature_frame(train).iloc[8760:]
    y = train.iloc[8760:]
    candidates: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    forecasts: list[np.ndarray] = []
    for leaves in (15, 31):

# Independent review and response

## Protocol review

A separate Claude Fable reviewer read the task, CSV and installed library APIs before the experiment produced test scores. Its verdict was that the design was sound, subject to the following concrete challenges.

1. **Darts early stopping is not validation MAPE by default.** Accepted. `ValidationMAPE` evaluates all 14 actual-history contexts at every training epoch, computes the median forecast MAPE over all 2,208 hours, and selects the best epoch. The public Darts prediction and callback forward path are checked for numerical agreement after refitting.
2. **Prophet's frozen fit forecasts validation from 1 to 92 days ahead.** Accepted. Prophet has no state update. Its validation scores select only its own seasonality mode and are not used to compare model classes. The transcript discloses this distinction.
3. **Recursive quantiles must share one median path; rolling variance may collapse; yearly lag drops the first year of feature targets.** Accepted. LightGBM recursively uses its median only, including for all five conditional quantile fits. Crossing correction preserves the median. Its training targets start after the 8,760-hour warmup; the source observations are not imputed or dropped from the dataset. The lag is exactly 8,760 hours, not weekday-aligned.
4. **Use the same training stride during selection and refit, and distinguish a quantile median from sampled forecasts.** Accepted. Both neural fits use stride 168, not a recent-only sample cap. All forecast origin hours are midnight UTC; N-BEATS retains its default 30 stacks. Quantiles come from the public likelihood-parameter prediction interface.
5. **Prophet's UTC calendar blurs local midnight and DST.** Accepted and disclosed. LightGBM's calendar features use Europe/Berlin; Prophet's regular input index and built-in holidays use UTC dates. No timezone shift or imputation is applied to the load grid.
6. **The final validation block is only 24 hours.** Accepted. Pool hours equally, not block means. Preserve per-block scores for inspection.
7. **Naive winner intervals require a separate calibration layer.** Accepted as a contingency. Native naive uncertainty remains absent. If it wins, validation signed-error quantiles supply separately labeled auxiliary intervals, never fitted on test.
8. **Rename the substituted model's machine key to transformer.** Partially accepted. Human-facing labels and `actual_class` explicitly say TransformerModel. Retain `patchtst` as the compatibility key because the requested metrics schema enumerates that key; it never means PatchTST actually ran.
9. **Bound SARIMA search and disclose Gaussian fixed-parameter intervals.** Accepted. Two explicit daily orders are tested on a weekly-pre-differenced series. No holiday regression is added to this classical comparator. This tests a different information representation, not whether SARIMA could benefit from known-calendar regressors.
10. **Explain bridge days, Jan 6's regional status, and mixed-unit metric bars.** Accepted. Jan 2–7 is called the remaining six days, not working days. Metric bars have a single dimensionless baseline-relative axis with raw %/MW labels; numerical tables remain the authoritative raw-scale view.

## Execution issue

The first run failed before any model selection or test scoring: statsmodels `low_memory=True` removed the predicted states required by `extend()`. The fixed implementation retains predicted states while omitting unused filtered/smoothing arrays. The original exception is preserved in `training_attempt1.log`. No model specification changed in response to test results.

## Code and results review

Pending final independent review and deterministic verification. This is not an approval claim.

1	# Independent review and response
2	
3	## Protocol review
4	
5	A separate Claude Fable reviewer read the task, CSV and installed library APIs before the experiment produced test scores. Its verdict was that the design was sound, subject to the following concrete challenges.
6	
7	1. **Darts early stopping is not validation MAPE by default.** Accepted. `ValidationMAPE` evaluates all 14 actual-history contexts at every training epoch, computes the median forecast MAPE over all 2,208 hours, and selects the best epoch. The public Darts prediction and callback forward path are checked for numerical agreement after refitting.
8	2. **Prophet's frozen fit forecasts validation from 1 to 92 days ahead.** Accepted. Prophet has no state update. Its validation scores select only its own seasonality mode and are not used to compare model classes. The transcript discloses this distinction.
9	3. **Recursive quantiles must share one median path; rolling variance may collapse; yearly lag drops the first year of feature targets.** Accepted. LightGBM recursively uses its median only, including for all five conditional quantile fits. Crossing correction preserves the median. Its training targets start after the 8,760-hour warmup; the source observations are not imputed or dropped from the dataset. The lag is exactly 8,760 hours, not weekday-aligned.
10	4. **Use the same training stride during selection and refit, and distinguish a quantile median from sampled forecasts.** Accepted. Both neural fits use stride 168, not a recent-only sample cap. All forecast origin hours are midnight UTC; N-BEATS retains its default 30 stacks. Quantiles come from the public likelihood-parameter prediction interface.
11	5. **Prophet's UTC calendar blurs local midnight and DST.** Accepted and disclosed. LightGBM's calendar features use Europe/Berlin; Prophet's regular input index and built-in holidays use UTC dates. No timezone shift or imputation is applied to the load grid.
12	6. **The final validation block is only 24 hours.** Accepted. Pool hours equally, not block means. Preserve per-block scores for inspection.
13	7. **Naive winner intervals require a separate calibration layer.** Accepted as a contingency. Native naive uncertainty remains absent. If it wins, validation signed-error quantiles supply separately labeled auxiliary intervals, never fitted on test.
14	8. **Rename the substituted model's machine key to transformer.** Partially accepted. Human-facing labels and `actual_class` explicitly say TransformerModel. Retain `patchtst` as the compatibility key because the requested metrics schema enumerates that key; it never means PatchTST actually ran.
15	9. **Bound SARIMA search and disclose Gaussian fixed-parameter intervals.** Accepted. Two explicit daily orders are tested on a weekly-pre-differenced series. No holiday regression is added to this classical comparator. This tests a different information representation, not whether SARIMA could benefit from known-calendar regressors.
16	10. **Explain bridge days, Jan 6's regional status, and mixed-unit metric bars.** Accepted. Jan 2–7 is called the remaining six days, not working days. Metric bars have a single dimensionless baseline-relative axis with raw %/MW labels; numerical tables remain the authoritative raw-scale view.
17	
18	## Execution issue
19	
20	The first run failed before any model selection or test scoring: statsmodels `low_memory=True` removed the predicted states required by `extend()`. The fixed implementation retains predicted states while omitting unused filtered/smoothing arrays. The original exception is preserved in `training_attempt1.log`. No model specification changed in response to test results.
21	
22	## Code and results review
23	
24	Pending final independent review and deterministic verification. This is not an approval claim.

1	from __future__ import annotations
2	
3	import time
4	import warnings
5	from typing import Any
6	
7	import numpy as np
8	import pandas as pd
9	from scipy.stats import norm
10	from statsmodels.tsa.statespace.sarimax import SARIMAX
11	
12	from common import ModelResult, QUANTILES, mape, validation_blocks
13	
14	SCALE = 10000.0
15	
16	
17	def fit_model(y: pd.Series, order: tuple[int, int, int], seasonal: tuple[int, int, int, int]) -> tuple[Any, list[str]]:
18	    weekly_difference = (y.diff(168).iloc[168:] / SCALE).asfreq("h")
19	    model = SARIMAX(weekly_difference, order=order, seasonal_order=seasonal,
20	                    trend="n", enforce_stationarity=True, enforce_invertibility=True,
21	                    concentrate_scale=True)
22	    # extend() needs predicted states; keep them but omit unused smoothing arrays.
23	    model.ssm.set_conserve_memory(memory_no_smoothing=True, memory_no_filtered=True)
24	    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
25	        warnings.simplefilter("always")
26	        fit = model.fit(disp=False, maxiter=60, low_memory=False)
27	        if not fit.mle_retvals.get("converged", False):
28	            fit = model.fit(start_params=fit.params, disp=False, maxiter=120, low_memory=False)
29	    messages = list(dict.fromkeys(str(w.message) for w in caught))
30	    if not fit.mle_retvals.get("converged", False):
31	        raise RuntimeError(f"SARIMA optimizer did not converge: {order}, {seasonal}")
32	    return fit, messages
33	
34	
35	def run(train: pd.Series, pretest: pd.Series, future: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> ModelResult:
36	    start = time.perf_counter()
37	    candidates: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
38	    forecasts: list[np.ndarray] = []
39	    warnings_seen: list[str] = []
40	    for order, seasonal in [((1, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0, 24)), ((2, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0, 24))]:
41	        fit, messages = fit_model(train, order, seasonal)
42	        warnings_seen.extend(messages)
43	        prediction: list[np.ndarray] = []
44	        for history, target in validation_blocks(pretest, len(train)):
45	            baseline = history.loc[target.index - pd.Timedelta(hours=168)].to_numpy()
46	            prediction.append(fit.get_forecast(len(target)).predicted_mean.to_numpy() * SCALE + baseline)
47	            # Only the state is updated as each validation block becomes history.
48	            observed_difference = pd.Series((target.to_numpy() - baseline) / SCALE, index=target.index).asfreq("h")
49	            fit = fit.extend(observed_difference)
50	        point = np.concatenate(prediction)
51	        score = mape(pretest.iloc[len(train):].to_numpy(), point)
52	        candidates.append({"order": list(order), "seasonal_order": list(seasonal),
53	                           "validation_mape_pct": score, "converged": True})
54	        forecasts.append(point)
55	        print(f"sarima {order}{seasonal} validation MAPE={score:.3f}%", flush=True)
56	    chosen = int(np.argmin([c["validation_mape_pct"] for c in candidates]))
57	    config = candidates[chosen]
58	    fit, messages = fit_model(pretest, tuple(config["order"]), tuple(config["seasonal_order"]))
59	    warnings_seen.extend(messages)
60	    distribution = fit.get_forecast(len(future))
61	    baseline = pretest.loc[future - pd.Timedelta(hours=168)].to_numpy()
62	    point = distribution.predicted_mean.to_numpy() * SCALE + baseline
63	    se = np.asarray(distribution.se_mean) * SCALE
64	    q = point[:, None] + se[:, None] * norm.ppf(QUANTILES)[None, :]
65	    params = {"order": config["order"], "seasonal_order": config["seasonal_order"],
66	              "weekly_pre_difference_hours": 168, "fixed_numeric_scale_mw": SCALE,
67	              "trend": "none", "concentrate_scale": True, "final_converged": True,
68	              "uncertainty": "Gaussian forecast-error variance; fixed fitted parameters"}
69	    return ModelResult("sarima", point, q, forecasts[chosen], params, candidates,
70	                       time.perf_counter() - start, {"optimizer_warnings": sorted(set(warnings_seen))})

15	def make_model(mode: str) -> Prophet:
16	    return Prophet(country_holidays="DE", daily_seasonality=True,
17	                   weekly_seasonality=True, yearly_seasonality=True,
18	                   seasonality_mode=mode, changepoint_prior_scale=0.01,
19	                   holidays_prior_scale=10.0, uncertainty_samples=600,
20	                   random_state=SEED)

23	def as_series(y: pd.Series) -> TimeSeries:
24	    return TimeSeries.from_series(y, fill_missing_dates=False, freq="h")

27	def run(train: pd.Series, pretest: pd.Series, future: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> ModelResult:
28	    start = time.perf_counter()
29	    logging.getLogger("cmdstanpy").setLevel(logging.WARNING)
30	    candidates: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
31	    forecasts: list[np.ndarray] = []
32	    validation_frame = pd.DataFrame({"ds": pretest.index[len(train):]})
33	    for mode in ("additive", "multiplicative"):
34	        model = make_model(mode)
35	        model.fit(as_series(train))
36	        # Prophet's time-only prediction is identical across the fixed-origin blocks.
37	        prediction = model.model.predict(validation_frame)["yhat"].to_numpy()
38	        score = mape(pretest.iloc[len(train):].to_numpy(), prediction)
39	        candidates.append({"seasonality_mode": mode, "validation_mape_pct": score})
40	        forecasts.append(prediction)
41	        print(f"prophet mode={mode} validation MAPE={score:.3f}%", flush=True)
42	    chosen = int(np.argmin([c["validation_mape_pct"] for c in candidates]))
43	    mode = candidates[chosen]["seasonality_mode"]
44	    final = make_model(mode)
45	    final.fit(as_series(pretest))
46	    frame = pd.DataFrame({"ds": future})
47	    prediction_frame = final.model.predict(frame)
48	    np.random.seed(SEED)
49	    samples = final.model.predictive_samples(frame)["yhat"]
50	    quantiles = np.quantile(samples, QUANTILES, axis=1).T
51	    components = prediction_frame[["ds", "trend", "weekly", "yearly", "daily", "holidays"]].copy()
52	    reference_dates = {
53	        "decomposition_trend": pd.date_range(pretest.index[0], pretest.index[-1], freq="D"),
54	        "decomposition_weekly": pd.date_range("2019-01-07", periods=168, freq="h"),
55	        "decomposition_yearly": pd.date_range("2019-01-01", periods=365, freq="D"),
56	    }
57	    decomposition = {}
58	    for key, dates in reference_dates.items():
59	        component = key.removeprefix("decomposition_")
60	        frame_ref = final.model.predict(pd.DataFrame({"ds": dates}))
61	        decomposition[key] = frame_ref[["ds", component]]
62	    params = {"country_holidays": "DE", "daily_seasonality": True,
63	              "weekly_seasonality": True, "yearly_seasonality": True,
64	              "seasonality_mode": mode, "changepoint_prior_scale": 0.01,
65	              "holidays_prior_scale": 10.0, "uncertainty_samples": 600,
66	              "seed": SEED, "calendar_timezone": "UTC (library-naive timestamps)",
67	              "uncertainty": "Prophet predictive samples, MAP parameters, mcmc_samples=0"}
68	    return ModelResult("prophet", prediction_frame["yhat"].to_numpy(), quantiles,
69	                       forecasts[chosen], params, candidates, time.perf_counter() - start,
70	                       {"components": components, **decomposition})

18	def calendar(index: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> pd.DataFrame:
19	    local = index.tz_localize("UTC").tz_convert("Europe/Berlin")
20	    holiday_dates = holidays.Germany(years=range(local.year.min(), local.year.max() + 1))
21	    return pd.DataFrame({

23	        "is_weekend": (local.dayofweek >= 5).astype(int),
24	        "is_public_holiday_de": [int(day in holiday_dates) for day in local.date],
25	    }, index=index)

28	def feature_frame(y: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
29	    x = calendar(y.index)
30	    for hours in (24, 168, 8760):
31	        x[f"lag_{hours}h"] = y.shift(hours)
32	    # Excluding the current target is stricter than merely excluding later rows.
33	    past = y.shift(1)
34	    for hours in (24, 168):
35	        x[f"rolling_mean_{hours}h"] = past.rolling(hours).mean()
36	        x[f"rolling_std_{hours}h"] = past.rolling(hours).std(ddof=1)
37	    return x[FEATURES]

40	def recursive_forecast(models: dict[float, Any], history: pd.Series,
41	                       future: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> np.ndarray:
42	    if len(history) < 8760 or future[0] != history.index[-1] + pd.Timedelta(hours=1):
43	        raise ValueError("Forecast must follow a complete history with all lags available.")
44	    if not future.equals(pd.date_range(future[0], periods=len(future), freq="h")):
45	        raise ValueError("Forecast timestamps must be contiguous hourly instants.")
46	    known: list[float] = history.to_list()
47	    time_values = calendar(future).to_numpy(dtype=float)
48	    quantiles = sorted(models)
49	    result = np.empty((len(future), len(quantiles)))
50	    for i in range(len(future)):
51	        row = list(time_values[i]) + [known[-lag] for lag in (24, 168, 8760)]
52	        for hours in (24, 168):
53	            window = np.asarray(known[-hours:])
54	            row.extend([float(window.mean()), float(window.std(ddof=1))])
55	        x = pd.DataFrame([row], columns=FEATURES)
56	        prediction = np.array([models[q].predict(x)[0] for q in quantiles])
57	        median_index = quantiles.index(0.5)
58	        median = prediction[median_index]
59	        result[i, :median_index] = np.minimum(np.sort(prediction[:median_index]), median)
60	        result[i, median_index] = median
61	        result[i, median_index + 1:] = np.maximum(np.sort(prediction[median_index + 1:]), median)
62	        known.append(float(median))

66	def estimator(leaves: int, quantile: float) -> LGBMRegressor:
67	    return LGBMRegressor(objective="quantile", alpha=quantile, n_estimators=300,
68	                         learning_rate=0.05, num_leaves=leaves, min_child_samples=60,
69	                         reg_lambda=1.0, random_state=SEED, n_jobs=1, verbosity=-1,
70	                         deterministic=True, force_col_wise=True)

73	def run(train: pd.Series, pretest: pd.Series, future: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> ModelResult:
74	    start = time.perf_counter()
75	    x = feature_frame(train).iloc[8760:]
76	    y = train.iloc[8760:]
77	    candidates: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
78	    forecasts: list[np.ndarray] = []
79	    for leaves in (15, 31):
80	        model = estimator(leaves, 0.5).fit(x, y)
81	        prediction = np.concatenate([recursive_forecast({0.5: model}, history, target.index)[:, 0]
82	                                     for history, target in validation_blocks(pretest, len(train))])
83	        score = mape(pretest.iloc[len(train):].to_numpy(), prediction)
84	        candidates.append({"num_leaves": leaves, "validation_mape_pct": score})
85	        forecasts.append(prediction)
86	        print(f"lightgbm leaves={leaves} validation MAPE={score:.3f}%", flush=True)
87	    chosen = int(np.argmin([c["validation_mape_pct"] for c in candidates]))
88	    leaves = candidates[chosen]["num_leaves"]
89	    final_x = feature_frame(pretest).iloc[8760:]
90	    models = {q: estimator(leaves, q).fit(final_x, pretest.iloc[8760:]) for q in QUANTILES}
91	    quantiles = recursive_forecast(models, pretest, future)
92	    importance = dict(zip(FEATURES, models[0.5].booster_.feature_importance(importance_type="gain").tolist()))
93	    params = {"num_leaves": leaves, "n_estimators": 300, "learning_rate": 0.05,
94	              "min_child_samples": 60, "reg_lambda": 1.0, "quantiles": QUANTILES,
95	              "seed": SEED, "features": FEATURES, "calendar_timezone": "Europe/Berlin",
96	              "training_feature_warmup_hours": 8760, "final_training_rows": len(final_x),
97	              "forecast_method": "recursive median, median-preserving lower/upper quantile rearrangement",
98	              "uncertainty": "conditional quantiles on recursive median predictor path"}
99	    return ModelResult("lightgbm", quantiles[:, 2], quantiles, forecasts[chosen], params,
100	                       candidates, time.perf_counter() - start, {"feature_importance_gain": importance})

19	class ValidationMAPE(Callback):
20	    def __init__(self, train: pd.Series, pretest: pd.Series, scale: float) -> None:
21	        super().__init__()
22	        blocks = validation_blocks(pretest, len(train))
23	        self.context = torch.tensor(np.stack([h.iloc[-HORIZON:].to_numpy() / scale for h, _ in blocks]),
24	                                    dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(-1)
25	        self.targets = pretest.iloc[len(train):].to_numpy()
26	        self.lengths = [len(target) for _, target in blocks]
27	        self.scale = scale
28	        self.best_mape = float("inf")
29	        self.best_epoch = 0
30	        self.best_prediction = np.empty(0)
31	        self.history: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
32	        self.stale = 0
33	        self.significant_best = float("inf")
34	
35	    def on_train_epoch_end(self, trainer: Trainer, pl_module: LightningModule) -> None:
36	        was_training = pl_module.training
37	        pl_module.eval()
38	        with torch.inference_mode():
39	            output = pl_module((self.context.to(pl_module.device), None, None))
40	            q = np.sort(output[:, :, 0, :].detach().cpu().numpy(), axis=2) * self.scale
41	        pl_module.train(was_training)
42	        point = np.concatenate([q[i, :length, 2] for i, length in enumerate(self.lengths)])
43	        score = mape(self.targets, point)
44	        epoch = trainer.current_epoch + 1
45	        self.history.append({"epoch": epoch, "validation_mape_pct": score})
46	        print(f"{type(pl_module).__name__} epoch={epoch} validation MAPE={score:.3f}%", flush=True)
47	        if score < self.best_mape:
48	            self.best_mape = score
49	            self.best_epoch = epoch
50	            self.best_prediction = point.copy()
51	        if score < self.significant_best - 0.01:
52	            self.significant_best = score
53	            self.stale = 0
54	        else:
55	            self.stale += 1
56	        if self.stale >= 5:
57	            trainer.should_stop = True

78	    return TimeSeries.from_series((y / scale).astype(np.float32), freq="h")

81	def run_neural(name: str, model_class: Any, architecture: dict[str, Any],
82	               train: pd.Series, pretest: pd.Series, future: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> ModelResult:
83	    start = time.perf_counter()
84	    torch.set_num_threads(4)
85	    torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)
86	    logging.getLogger("pytorch_lightning").setLevel(logging.WARNING)
87	    seed_everything(SEED, workers=True, verbose=False)
88	    train_scale = float(train.mean())
89	    callback = ValidationMAPE(train, pretest, train_scale)
90	    model = make_model(model_class, 30, [callback], f"{name}_selection", architecture)
91	    model.fit(series(train, train_scale), stride=168, verbose=False,
92	              dataloader_kwargs={"num_workers": 0})
93	    selected_epochs = callback.best_epoch
94	    if selected_epochs < 1:
95	        raise RuntimeError("Neural validation callback did not run.")
96	    del model
97	    gc.collect()
98	    # This is a fresh fit, not continued optimization on validation targets.
99	    seed_everything(SEED, workers=True, verbose=False)
100	    final_scale = float(pretest.mean())
101	    final = make_model(model_class, selected_epochs, [], f"{name}_final", architecture)
102	    final_series = series(pretest, final_scale)
103	    final.fit(final_series, stride=168, verbose=False, dataloader_kwargs={"num_workers": 0})
104	    distribution = final.predict(len(future), series=final_series,
105	                                 predict_likelihood_parameters=True, num_samples=1, verbose=False)
106	    if not distribution.time_index.equals(future):
107	        raise ValueError("Darts returned an unexpected test forecast index.")
108	    quantiles = np.sort(distribution.values(), axis=1).astype(float) * final_scale
109	    # The callback's fast forward path must agree with the public Darts predictor.
110	    final.model.eval()
111	    context = torch.tensor(final_series.values()[-168:], dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(0)
112	    with torch.inference_mode():
113	        raw = final.model((context, None, None))[0, :, 0, :].cpu().numpy()
114	    np.testing.assert_allclose(np.sort(raw, axis=1) * final_scale, quantiles, rtol=2e-5, atol=0.1)
115	    params = {"actual_class": model_class.__name__, "input_chunk_length": 168,
116	              "output_chunk_length": 168, "max_epochs": 30, "selected_epochs": selected_epochs,
117	              "early_stopping_metric": "validation MAPE of rearranged median, all 2208 hours",
118	              "early_stopping_patience": 5, "early_stopping_min_delta_pct": 0.01,
119	              "training_stride_hours": 168, "batch_size": 32, "learning_rate": 0.001,
120	              "gradient_clip_val": 1.0, "likelihood": "QuantileRegression",
121	              "quantiles": QUANTILES, "seed": SEED, "accelerator": "cpu", "threads": 4,
122	              "train_scale_mw": train_scale, "final_scale_mw": final_scale,
123	              "final_training_windows": (len(pretest) - 336) // 168 + 1,
124	              **architecture}
125	    if name == "nbeats":
126	        params.update({"generic_architecture": True, "num_stacks": 30, "num_blocks": 1,
127	                       "num_layers": 4, "layer_widths": 256, "expansion_coefficient_dim": 5})
128	    else:
129	        params["substitution"] = "Darts 0.41.0 has no PatchTSTModel; TransformerModel is an actual transformer, not TSMixer."
130	    result = ModelResult(name, quantiles[:, 2], quantiles, callback.best_prediction,
131	                         params, callback.history, time.perf_counter() - start,
132	                         {"callback_public_predict_equivalence": True})
133	    del final
134	    gc.collect()
135	    return result
136

1	# Forecasting bake-off plan
2	
3	1. Verify `opsd_de_load.csv`, the prescribed interpreter, and installed model source. Use a fixed origin for every 168-hour forecast. Data-derived future features must use predictions, not future observations.
4	2. Write consumer tests in `code/test_study.py`, shared contracts in `code/common.py`, then the six named model modules. Fit initial coefficients and scalers only on data before 2019-10-01. Score the 13 complete validation weeks and final 24 hours without updating coefficients. Earlier validation observations may update forecast contexts at later origins.
5	3. Select SARIMA orders, Prophet prior strength, LightGBM tree complexity, and neural epoch count by validation MAPE. Refit fresh models and scalers on all data before 2020-01-01. No test values are arguments to model-fitting functions.
6	4. Produce test forecasts and five quantiles where supported. Use analytic SARIMA intervals, Prophet posterior-predictive samples, and neural quantile regression. LightGBM has five quantile fits, including the extra 0.025 and 0.975 needed for a 95% interval. Its recursive intervals are conditional on the median path and omit propagation of predictor uncertainty.
7	5. `code/forecast.py` orchestrates training and writes `metrics.json`, `metrics.csv`, forecast and validation evidence, all required figures, and `transcript.md`. Preserve raw data and write only under this directory. Use `../../.venv/bin/python`, no installs.
8	6. Verify every metric from the saved forecasts, examine the figure renders, and request independent review. Record failures and departures honestly. No commits or publication.
9	
10	## Assumptions fixed before seeing test scores
11	
12	- One forecast issued at 2020-01-01 00:00 UTC covers the entire week. Observed load during that week cannot enter predictors.
13	- Validation covers all 2,208 hours, weighted equally, rather than choosing favorable weeks.
14	- Daily SARIMA does not automatically learn weekly seasonality. An explicit 168-hour difference supplies weekly structure; daily residual orders are selected on validation. For horizons up to 168 hours the inverse difference uses only known load.
15	- PatchTST is not present in Darts 0.41.0. Use its actual `TransformerModel`, not TSMixer, and label the substitution everywhere visible while retaining the requested `patchtst` machine key.
16	- Neural training uses full default N-BEATS stacks, 168-hour input/output lengths, a recorded 168-hour training stride, at most 30 epochs, and validation-MAPE early stopping. Sparse windows bound compute without shortening the historical span.

All six models have completed validation and fresh pre-test refits. LightGBM wins the held-out week with **3.96% MAPE**, followed by Prophet at **7.48%**; the weekly naive baseline scores **12.78%**.

The holiday pattern is more nuanced than the prompt anticipated: the neural models struggle most on Jan 1, while the naive and SARIMA forecasts suffer later because they repeat Christmas-week and New Year’s Eve load. LightGBM’s empirical coverage is **86.3% for its nominal 80% interval** and **98.8% for its nominal 95% interval**, though these conditional intervals do not propagate uncertainty through the recursive features.

content.thinking:
All six models finished training quickly, which makes sense given the small window count from the stride and batch size. Now I'm checking the scaling logic in nbeats.py, where training uses the mean of the train set but refit uses the mean of the pretest set for the final scale.

I'm tracing how the callback constructs the forward pass input tuple for NBEATS and comparing it against the public predict path, since the assertion at line 114 checks their equivalence with a tight tolerance. Since training completed without any errors, that assertion must have passed, giving confidence the callback's forward call is unpacking the input tuple correctly and matches the model's actual prediction behavior.

I also confirm the early stopping logic worked as intended—NBEATS ran 28 epochs and stopped after five stale epochs past its best score, and Transformer similarly stopped at epoch 17 after peaking at epoch 12—then each model gets refit using only the number of epochs up to its best score rather than the full budget.

Refitting slightly changes the step count per epoch since the pretest data is larger than the training data, but this is a minor and disclosable discrepancy. Scaling is consistent too: model selection uses training-only scalers, while the final refit uses scalers fit on the combined pretest data, which is the correct approach as long as it's documented.

Callback windows pulling from validation history are permitted by the protocol since they're just context updates, and both validation and test MAPE calculations sort the quantile predictions before taking the middle element as the median, so the methodology stays consistent across both evaluation stages. The quantile regression training runs without a validation series during the final fit.

Now I'm checking how Darts handles the stride parameter during training — specifically whether windows are anchored from the end of the series, which would determine if all forecast origins actually land on midnight UTC as claimed in the review. This matters for verifying that specific disclosure claim, though it doesn't affect the core correctness of the approach.

I'm working through the SARIMA setup: differencing the series by 168 hours (one week) before fitting a seasonal SARIMA model, then reconstructing forecasts by adding back the baseline from one week prior. Since the horizon is limited to 168 hours, that baseline always falls within known history, so the reconstruction is valid.

I'm also checking how the statsmodels `extend` method works for updating fitted state when new observations arrive, and whether the memory-conservation settings I'm using (`memory_no_smoothing`, `memory_no_filtered`) are compatible with `extend`'s reliance on predicted state and its covariance from the end of the previous fit.

Working out k_states here confirms memory isn't a real concern, so that explains why the low_memory=True attempt failed — it enables MEMORY_CONSERVE which drops predicted states, matching what review.md documents. I should also verify that extend correctly builds the new index by appending to the original date range with matching frequency, since that's needed for get_forecast on the extended result to line up properly.

The training run confirms this works fine — it completed without error and gave a plausible SARIMA validation MAPE of 4.76%. On the interval calculation, since the seasonal baseline for h ≤ 168 is a known historical value, the level forecast variance equals the differenced forecast variance, which is correct. The overall model is effectively SARIMA with a 168-period seasonal difference, and now I'm setting up the final refit on the full pretest data.

Moving to Prophet, I'm using the underlying prophet object's predict method on the validation frame after fitting on the training series, then refitting on the full pretest set and generating 600 predictive samples to compute quantiles across the 168-hour horizon, seeding the random state beforehand since Prophet relies on global numpy randomness. Now I'm turning to how the final candidate model gets selected based on these results.

Checking whether Prophet's DE holidays are national-only via the holidays package — confirmed, and noting holiday windows align to UTC midnight boundaries. The fit ran fine on 43,824 hourly rows in 19 seconds with default changepoints. Now moving to LightGBM, where I'm looking at how lag features are built via shift and rolling windows.

Verifying that the rolling mean window matches between training (past values shifted) and recursive forecasting (using the last known values through t-1), and confirming lag features are consistently defined in both. I'm also checking that the calendar feature construction handles timezone conversion identically in training and recursion, and now looking at how public holiday flags are matched against local dates.

The training pipeline drops the first 8760 rows since lag_8760h produces NaNs there, then uses feature_frame on the remaining pretest rows, and I'm noting that the model selection step only picks based on the median quantile before refitting all five quantiles with the chosen hyperparameters on pretest data. I'm now examining the quantile rearrangement logic that sorts and clips lower quantiles to maintain proper ordering.

The hyperparameter grid is narrow but workable — fixed estimators and learning rate, only leaf count varies between two options, with deterministic settings for reproducibility. Using alpha=0.5 as the quantile objective correctly gives median regression as the point forecast. I check that the recursive forecast has enough history for validation blocks, then move to reviewing the naive baseline's validation window.

For the naive baseline, taking the last 168 hours and slicing the first N to match the target length correctly recovers the "same hour last week" values, so the Dec 31 predictions correctly reference late-December history. I confirm the point predictions align with the shifted timestamps.

Then I look at how forecast.py handles module path conflicts to prevent its local prophet.py file from shadowing the actual prophet package import that darts depends on, checking whether the sys.path manipulation correctly resolves to the site-packages version.

I also notice a fragility: patchtst.py depends on nbeats being imported first under a specific module name, which only works because of the loading order in the orchestrator script, and test_study.py's direct imports only avoid the same shadowing issue because it happens not to import prophet.py itself — a minor but real risk if that file changes.

Checking the metrics logic, the January 1 mask correctly uses UTC-normalized timestamps, and the probabilistic metrics function correctly picks quantile columns for 80% and 95% coverage intervals with the standard pinball loss formula.

Naive models don't need a refit-on-train+val step since none is required, and the validation blocks loop calls extend on the SARIMA fit even after the final block—harmless but unnecessary. Looking at the N-BEATS runtime, 28 epochs over 246 windows at batch size 32 means only 224 gradient steps total for a 30-stack model, which is quite few given the stride-168 sampling means every training epoch sees windows anchored at the same hour.

I realize this stride creates a subtle issue: since windows are anchored to the end of the series and step by exactly one week, every training origin falls on the same weekday. Working through the dates, all selection-training origins land on Tuesdays at 00:00 UTC while the actual test origin is a Wednesday, meaning the model never trained on that specific weekday-of-week pattern.

The real issue is the model class gets heavily constrained though a fixed weekday phase, and stride 168 collapses training to just 246 samples with "epochs" being only 8 gradient steps — nowhere near the intended stride-1 scale of ~41k windows/epoch. Given the tiny 18s compute budget, stride 24 would have given 7x more training windows at only ~2 min cost, so I'd flag this as the main methodological weakness and recommend either disclosure or switching to stride 24.

Since re-training now would happen after seeing validation scores, that's protocol-legal only if the decision isn't test-informed — the test forecasts already exist in the artifacts but haven't been scored yet, so I should present this as a disclosure requirement and an option rather than mandate a re-run. I also want to double check how Darts anchors stride windows at dataset construction, and verify the training window formula and the callback structure feeding context into the PLForecastingModule.

I'm tracing through the NBEATS forward signature to confirm how it unpacks the input tuple — since training completed successfully, whatever unpacking scheme is used clearly matched the data shape, and the earlier assertion also passed, so I'm treating this as empirically verified. I'm also confirming that deterministic algorithms are safely enabled on CPU, and that seeding is applied consistently before both model selection and the final refit.

The refit should get a fresh initialization identical to the selection run since the seed and architecture match, only the training data differs, which seems correct. I'm checking that `random_state` and the trainer's deterministic flag are set properly, that `save_result` writes the forecast CSV with sorted quantile columns matching what `read_results` expects, that the metrics calculation is safe since all actuals are positive, and that the data loading is strict enough to catch issues early. I'm now moving on to check the `ModelResult` validation logic.

For NBEATS, the validation point uses the callback's best prediction, which reflects the selection model's forecasts at its best epoch, so that looks fine for reporting purposes. The Prophet run stores extra DataFrames like components and decomposition, exported as CSVs, which also seems fine. For SARIMA validation, I'm checking whether the baseline uses previously observed values from earlier validation blocks, since history includes prior blocks, and that seems like allowed context. The test point's baseline pulls from the pretest week of December 25-31, which looks okay too. Now I'm examining whether `fit.extend()` correctly inherits the `conserve_memory` setting when cloning the model and reinitializing state before smoothing.

I confirm that `extend()` produces forecasts from the end of the new endogenous data only, using the filtered state carried forward from previous data, effectively updating state without touching the fitted coefficients, which is the desired behavior. I also verify that the weekly difference calculation and the validation loop's baseline subtraction are consistent with how the differencing was originally defined. Now I'm moving on to review the transcript and report structure.

I check that Prophet's validation frame correctly uses the pretest index following the training set with a naive timezone. I verify that the N-BEATS callback contexts are built from validation blocks using the last 168 hours of each block's history, scaled by the training scale factor. I confirm early stopping on validation MAPE and refitting on train plus validation are both implemented, and that the test window stays untouched throughout — the future index and pretest set correctly exclude it, with the full dataset reserved only for final reporting. I also verify the forecast script pins the train/pretest split at the correct row counts, and I'm now considering a potential violation to flag.

I note the prompt asked for a LightGBM quantile objective at three levels (0.1, 0.5, 0.9), but the implementation actually fits five, which is a superset and therefore fine. For N-BEATS, I confirm the default stack configuration is used since an empty parameter dict was passed, though batch size and learning rate were chosen a priori without validation, which I consider acceptable. For the Transformer, I flag that its architecture (d_model 32, fewer layers, smaller feed-forward dimension) is a reduced configuration chosen upfront rather than selected via validation on test data — worth disclosing even though it doesn't violate the no-test-leakage rule. I also check that PatchTST correctly merges its architecture parameters into the params dict.

Now I want to quickly grep the darts source for stride anchoring and forward signature details, check how statsmodels handles the conserve-memory option during extend, review the test_green.log and test_red.log contents, and glance at the artifacts listing without doing any actual scoring — I'll batch all these checks together.

I've reviewed all nine in-scope files along with review.md, plan.md, and training.log—training is fully complete. Before writing up findings, I need to verify three facts I can't infer from code alone: how Darts anchors strided training windows, whether statsmodels' `extend` path inherits the conserve-memory setting, and what the test logs actually show, so I'll check each of these now.

def time_axis(ax: Any, dates: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> None:
    import matplotlib.dates as mdates
    ax.set_xlim(dates[0], dates[-1])
    ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.DayLocator())
    ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%b %d"))
    ax.set_xlabel("Date (UTC)")

def overview(data: pd.Series) -> None:
    import matplotlib.dates as mdates
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 6))
    fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.09, right=0.98, bottom=0.14, top=0.87)
    ax.plot(data.index, data, color="#c9c9c9", linewidth=0.28, label="Observed hourly load")
    test = data.loc["2020-01-01":"2020-01-07"]
    ax.axvspan(test.index[0], test.index[-1], color="#c53030", alpha=0.22)
    ax.plot(test.index, test, color="#c53030", linewidth=0.65, label="Held-out test week")
    ax.annotate("Test: Jan 1–7, 2020 (168 h)", xy=(test.index[84], 74000),
                xytext=(0.58, 0.96), textcoords="axes fraction", fontsize=10,
                arrowprops={"arrowstyle": "->", "color": "#444444", "lw": 0.8})
    ax.set_title("German national electricity load: the test week in context", pad=18)
    ax.set_xlabel("Year (UTC)")
    ax.set_ylabel("Load (MW)")
    ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.YearLocator())
    ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%Y"))
    ax.set_xlim(data.index[0], data.index[-1])
    ax.set_ylim(28000, 83000)
    ax.legend(loc="lower left", ncol=2, fontsize=9)
    fig.text(0.09, 0.025, "OPSD / ENTSO-E  |  50,400 hourly observations  |  Later 2020 values are shown here only, never used for fitting.", fontsize=9)
    save_figure(fig, "01_overview.png")


def forecast_comparison(test: pd.Series, results: list[ModelResult], rows: dict[str, dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
    import matplotlib.dates as mdates
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(11, 6), sharex=True, sharey=True)
    fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.08, right=0.985, bottom=0.15, top=0.82, hspace=0.4, wspace=0.12)
    minimum = min(test.min(), *(r.point.min() for r in results))
    maximum = max(test.max(), *(r.point.max() for r in results))
    for ax, result in zip(axes.flat, results):
        ax.plot(test.index, test, color="black", linewidth=1.3)
        ax.plot(test.index, result.point, color=COLORS[result.name], linewidth=1.65, linestyle="--")
        ax.axvspan(test.index[0], pd.Timestamp("2020-01-02"), color="#777777", alpha=0.06)
        ax.set_title(f"{SHORT_LABELS[result.name]}  |  {rows[result.name]['mape_test_pct']:.2f}% MAPE", fontsize=10)
        ax.set_ylim(minimum - 2500, maximum + 2500)
        ax.set_xlim(test.index[0], test.index[-1])
        ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.DayLocator(interval=2))
        ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%b %d"))

    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

    days = pd.date_range("2020-01-01", periods=7, freq="D")

    for row in ranked:

        values.append([mape(test.to_numpy()[test.index.normalize() == day],
                            p[test.index.normalize() == day]) for day in days])
    matrix = pd.DataFrame(values, index=[r["name"] for r in ranked], columns=days.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"))
    matrix.to_csv(ROOT / "artifacts" / "per_day_mape.csv", index_label="model")
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 6))
    fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.24, right=0.88, bottom=0.2, top=0.82)
    image = ax.imshow(matrix.to_numpy(), cmap="Blues", vmin=0, vmax=max(40.0, matrix.to_numpy().max()), aspect="auto")
    ax.set_xticks(range(7), [day.strftime("%b %d\n%a") for day in days], fontsize=8)
    ax.set_yticks(range(6), [SHORT_LABELS[r["name"]].replace("Seasonal naive", "Naive") for r in ranked], fontsize=9)

    ax.grid(False)
    for i in range(6):
        for j in range(7):
            value = matrix.iloc[i, j]
            ax.text(j, i, f"{value:.1f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=9,
